newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Nov 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Nov 13.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- US-EU PUSH FOR TRANSATLANTIC TRADE BOOST

Top business figures from Europe and the USA, including representatives of British Telecom, Volvo, Ford and Philips, met in Spain over the weekend, and prepared an action plan to boost transatlantic trade by cutting regulations and harmonising product standards. They intend to lobby the US administration and the European Commission to this effect.
-- CARADON'S COHEN TO LEAVE IN SHAKE-UP

Caradon's former finance director. Daniel Cohen, now chairing the group's European division, is to leave the group as part of a management reorganization expected to involve the loss of up to 2,000 of the 26,000 jobs. The review follows the September profits warning.
-- CHIPS KESWICK IN HAMBROS STEP UP

Sir Chips Keswick, deputy chairman of Hambros, will step up to the new position of group chief executive in a restructuring to be announced with results on Wednesday. The restructuring is seen as a sign that the group wishes to remain independent.
THE TIMES
-- INVESTMENT OFFENDERS MAY HAVE TO PUBLICISE THEIR SINS

The Personal Investment Authority is planning to next year introduce individual contracts between companies advising on pensions and selling investments. Such contracts would enable the PIA to fine individual salesmen and expel them from the industry. It would also bring it into step with the Securities and Futures Authority. It faces fierce industry opposition to the plan.
-- CBI WARNS AGAINST TAX GIVEAWAY

The Confederation of British Industry has warned the Chancellor against taking risks with public borrowing in a 'giveaway' Budget. Business leaders want only limited or no tax cuts at all, according to a CBI survey. At its annual conference today, the CBI will say tax cuts can only be made if funded by 'credible' public spending cuts.
-- BLUNDER MAY COST THAMES 2 MILLION POUNDS STG

A series of billing errors may cost Thames Water up to 2 million pounds stg in an out of court settlement with three customers in a late-payment dispute. Thames dropped the case after being criticised by a judge for unlawfully threatening to disconnect a sewerage customer's water supply.
THE GUARDIAN
-- BLAIR SETS TERMS FOR 'NEW ERA'

Tony Blair will today promise British industry a 'new era of positive relations' with Labour at the CBI conference. He will pledge that Labour will not try to pick winners or impose penal rates of taxation, but will nonetheless insist on a national minimum wage and adhesion to the EU Social Chapter.
-- REDWOOD ROCKS EURO BOAT
John Redwood intends to whip up anti-Europe sentiment at a fringe meeting of the pro-Europe CBI conference. CBI leaders said they would welcome a full debate on the issues.
-- BOEING BEGINS DELAYED DELIVERY OF 2.2 BILLION POUND BA ORDER
British Airways will today take delivery of the first of the 15 Boeing 777s ordered from Boeing, and delayed for six weeks after testing problems. It is thought unlikely they will seek compensation.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- SALOMAN BLOW TO STOCK EXCHANGE

The Stock Exchange is to suffer a further blow this week when Saloman Brothers announces it is abandoning London for trading European equities. Similar decisions are also said to be imminent from several other international houses, including Lehman Brothers, providing final confirmation that the challenge by Seaq International, the Exchange's trading facility, to Europe is over, after criticism of being out of date and inefficient.
-- LANG VOWS PROGRESS ON COMPETITION LAW

Board of Trade president Ian Lang yesterday promised that his department would find ways around delays to a reform of competition policy. The Government has been planning changes to eliminate restrictive practices since 1993, and methods to take action could include private members' bills, inserts in other bills or avoidance altogether of primary legislation.
-- NFC FACES LEGAL ACTION OVER PENSION SURPLUS

The rail freight business privatized 13 years ago under a management buyout has been threatened with legal action over allegedly short-changing 25,000 pensioners and their dependents. NFC holds a 263 million pound stg surplus in the pension fund, which former employees should be partly used to increase benefits to pensioners.
